title: Conformal Segmentation in Industrial Surface Defect Detection with Statistical Guarantees
mechanism: Conformal risk control on a calibration split sets a pixel threshold so the expected test error rate (e.g. missed defect fraction) is bounded by a chosen risk level.
adaptation: Benchmark operating point: calibrate crack threshold on val + F51 for expected relR@2 >= 0.90 and report the precision it costs; same for inactive area fraction (severity); test whether the guarantee holds on E1 under shift.
evidence: R: Mask R-CNN on industrial defects, test error stays under the risk level across calibration/test ratios.
min_experiment: No training: calibrate on val + F51, report realised relR@2 and precision on clean-49 test and E1; kill (as a method) if realised E1 recall falls below target by > 0.1, which is itself a benchmark finding.
prior_overlap: Logit bias and per-module thresholds were tried (threshold choice); conformal guarantee is new and aimed at the benchmark, not the score.
